subject.title: fix(cron): allow timeoutSeconds: 0 for no-timeout mode

question: Should the Control UI expose the gateway's `timeoutSeconds: 0` no-timeout sentinel, and what proof/test bar should this PR meet before merge?
rationale: The backend contract already accepts zero, but UI exposure lets normal users disable the cron wall-clock safety timeout, so automation cannot accept that availability tradeoff without maintainer intent.

options.title: Expose zero with proof
options.body: Refresh the branch to the moved cron UI files, update regression tests, and require real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Keep UI positive-only
options.body: Close or redirect this PR and leave zero-timeout creation to lower-level API surfaces until maintainers want a no-timeout UI affordance.

options.title: Expose only with warning
options.body: Require an explicit UI warning or confirmation before allowing no-timeout cron jobs from the form.

recommendation.title: Expose zero with proof
recommendation.body: Refresh the branch to the moved cron UI files, update regression tests, and require real behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The original cron edit parity work introduced the affected Control UI timeout behavior and tests.
